Positive: I attend a uni that wants to commemorate 100 years of women being able to study Law (with actual Law students as actors too) AND today I was emailed about Art events that are going down at the Law building that I can bring my little pieces to.

I emailed my Medical lecturer with questions surrounding the Non-Assessed essay. He proceeded to ask for me in the middle of the lecture (fully packed) for audience participation. (I didn’t answer) I’ve never wanted to disappear as much. Looks like I won’t be doing it again.

-Divisiveness for families,an all-encompassing US v THEM (either side). -The fact that I didn’t get to vote for something I study and will incorporate into my career. Whilst people that could have, didn’t. -Destroying my nation internally and externally #WhatBrexitMeansToMe

I understand why the courts deal with Domestic Violence in the Civil and Criminal courts, but it makes me angry that more Domestic Abusers are given orders, than prison time. I’d argue it has similarities to ABH, GBH? Maybe I’m too biased in how things (didn’t) happen for me.

Breaking into little bits per day. I have 6 modules, so other than attending lectures, each day has a separate amount of time and topic (1-3 hours) whereupon I go over; cases, Law Review/Journals, recent Reform etc. I have either Saturday (as I’m working) or Sunday to rest.

I’m rallying around every family member to make sure they are signed up to vote. Not big stuff, but I didn’t get to vote in the massive Brexit one last time and thus, I’m taking full advantage of this General Election vote. Friday the 13th for the new leader though...
Coming home for the half-term and being greeted by an ACCEPTANCE letter for Mini-Pupillage has made the 5+ hour train journey worth it. Beyond euphoric right now.

This year will end with me having secured both a Vacation Scheme and a Mini-Pupillage. (As well as work within NGOs.) I’m not generally proud of myself or my abilities, but the idea that the hard work is paying off is really warming.
People-Watching: Students, obviously procrastinating, swivelling back and forth on spinny chairs in time to the Monsters: INC opening credits, in one of the lecture hallways. I love uni.

Really unusual it seems, but all the Constitutional Law modules from the former two years alongside Jurisprudence and International Human Rights from my Third (this year). Any module that I can really grapple with argument wise.

I’ve been running through a copious amount of articles on First Gen students recently. I stumbled across “perceived as different in home and at uni, first generation students often feel they don’t belong to either”. Since Year 1 LLB, I thought it was just me. I’m not defective.

I’m pleased there’s a little clan of us that’s in the same boat- I’ve been hit by several instances this year, where it has been obvious that I was different to the peers around me. Law school is alright once you get used to the workload (I just treat it like a full time job).

Going over Domestic Violence in Family Law has made me angrier than I assumed I would be. Not only on account of the active parent that didn’t stop things going on at home, but also my Mum, the passive parent, that neither stepped in, nor went to the external authorities.

Then there’s knowing we could have put Criminal proceedings forward, but never did because I never had the opportunity given, so we went the Civil route which engineered a restraining order that was breached at least 3 times and left the abuser going around the neighbourhood.

My uni has put a Scheme up for Law students whereupon the State School educated (parents with no BA education) can sign up to be considered for a month-marshalling a judge in an inn of court. I’ve put my name down. Time and time again I’m proven right in coming to this uni.
It makes me seethe how this is known as the “Brexit Election” when poverty like this is being swept under the carpet. Where are the debates surrounding this?!

I was in exactly the same position the last time we had a major vote (2016). I’m doing it for the 17-year-old that wanted to vote on behalf of my future (and my career) and every other “on the cusp” individual that is deprived of that same vote this time around.

I use Lesbian to push away creepers rather than Bisexual (even then it’s sometimes pushed), but then I feel like I’m taking an identity which isn’t mine. A NO is clearly a message in itself and should stand that way.

This wasn’t just “The Brexit Election”, this was for 4.1 million kids in breadline conditions, our NHS and the environmental crisis. The worst thing is indifference. There’s more integrity in voting for an unpopular party than just not voting at all. Very incensed right now.

I found out earlier this week that my mark for the Jurisprudence Non-Assessed work was 65-67% (2:1). I’m really aiming for 70+ in this module because I know I’m capable, so I’m putting everything in and taking on board all advice given. It’s always at the cost of health though.

My best Christmas present was given to me today when my ex landlord emailed me to state that I don’t have to pay rent from January 2020 onwards and my contract has been terminated because I haven’t been in the property since last February. A big weight has been lifted.

POSITIVE: All my Postgraduate applications have been sent off to the universities I’ve selected. Big weight lifted, but now it’s the wait for conditions as well as potential rejections and getting set to get the conditional LLB marks for Final Year. Pre-2020 stress is real.
Positive: I wanted to branch out for my art exhibition I’m doing in January at my uni. It didn't turn out terrible.

Positive: Today I met an Irish solicitor that swore like a sailor when describing the trial we were both attending. I like the juxtaposition-of the orthodox courtroom and the profanity-spouting legal professional. He and it made me laugh, which I haven’t been doing a lot of.

Positive: I’ve just received confirmation of a conditional offer to one of my LLM Human Rights Law programmes. Given that it’s a 21 day turn around and it’s been Christmas, I’ve received this one really quickly. At least one uni wants me🥳

Mini-Pupillage Day 4: I’ve had the excellent opportunity all week to shadow a Criminal Litigation Barrister in court. Including the verdict today. Tomorrow, I have my final day working in Chambers,which is my first introduction into the inner workings of the realm of barristers.

Mini-Pupillage Final Day: It’s been an insightful week, full of moments that made me realise how integral law is to society and to the protection of individuals. We have also retained 17th century customs here that makes the whole affair “incredibly English”. Loved my week.

As part of my LLB, Property Law. -Needing confirmation that your property means more than you do?! Property Law is for you🙄 I found the material dry too. alongside the cynical outlook of the module itself.
Positive: Two of my Five universities that I have applied to for my Master’s have now offered me places on their LLM for Human Rights Law.
I’m the first in my immediate family to be receiving a Bachelors and hopefully next year, a Masters degree from university. Being First Gen is the accomplishment I’m most proud of.
Positive: My cat’s kidney levels are down to “normal range” and he is back home. I have also received an Assessment day in order to be put forward to work abroad voluntary, post exams in May.

When I’m asked about my greatest academic accomplishment,I always have to suppress the answer of “I helped to and convinced my sister to write an essay on Gnomeo and Juliet as a means of satirising Shakespeare’s content with garden gnomes and she got a 2:1” But it is the truth.

I can hear the first “Brexit fireworks” outside my halls and I am so sad. Sad about our laws being scrapped. Sad about trade. Small businesses. International relations. Migrants. I know so many other people I’ve had discussions with over the past 4 years that are likely sad too.
Moreover, we are likely set to lose the Europeans Convention on Human Rights. It took us decades to get unified doctrine and now it’s just being scrapped.
Positive: I’ve been accepted to go overseas as part of VSO, (First Stage pass) after the assessment day I had on Wednesday🥳

Positive: I got my tattoo. Starry Night- Van Gogh
Positive: My presentation from last term that was ripped apart in class still got a 2:1 mark. Knowing I did 70% of the work and still did ok is a really nice feeling.

On recommendation, I am reading ‘Limbo’ by Alfred Lubrano. If there are any First Gen law students feeling like they don’t belong to blue collar origins or white collar peers/job opportunities, this book is amazing. I feel heard for the first time since beginning my degree.

Positive: Last day at work presents and thank you card. It’s sad to walk away, but I didn’t want to continue and become embittered due to factors outside of the work itself.

Positive: My Research Credit (12 pages) has been sent off for marking. I’ve been rewording and restructuring over the past 3 weeks to (try to) get it to a high standard. A dissertation allows for input from lecturers, but a RC doesn’t, so I have no idea if it’s more 40% or 70%🙃
I heard about it today. He died on the 20th, but Corona overshadowed his death completely. Dolly Parton’s tribute was lovely though.

Positive: Disregarding the “take home exams” I have throughout late April and May, I have submitted my last essay for my LLB degree🥳 The essay I’m proudest of to be honest, on account of the adversity and weirdness of this term and overall academic year.

Positive: My Best Friend and myself swapped bakes we made for each other (from a distance naturally). Brownies were exchanged for butterfly buns. She’s also agreed to attend my “graduation” in my back garden, if we are allowed out in July, as my uni one has been cancelled.

My First of Final Year LLB Exams is tomorrow morning. The night before is always a burst of nerves that I’ve studied the wrong thing/ I will get below what I need to progress. I’ve worked my arse off for these exams, but you never know.
POSITIVE: Final LLB Exam is done🥳 My Law degree is complete (unless I have to resit anything)

My concentration has diminished considerably post-exams. I’m used to finishing books within the same day and now I can barely go 100 pages without needing to walk around. The wait between sitting exams and getting the results has led to a nervous energy I can’t quell.

Little Things: There’s a case I’ve been reading over where a man was refused “trial by combat” with the plaintiff. (Case from the 2010s) This man had put this request in writing, which was sent to the opposition as a “reasonable” option. The human race is ridiculous.
15. Over the course of my GCSEs, my mental health went down its first downward spiral. I was told by my parents that it was “all in your head”. 2 years later, I was diagnosed with Depression.
An acerbic middle-aged wreck of a man seeks out the purity of a teenager. There’s a fire. She marries him.

100%. It meant that I surpassed my family history of education (on paper) at the age of 16, I went outside of my home town and that I am now pursuing my Master of Laws course. It is absolutely disgraceful and contemptible that those similar opportunities have been taken away.
Positive: I have an interview with GICJ late August (Centre for Justice). I could potentially be going to Geneva after my LLM programme has ended, if I’m successful in the next stage of selection🤞

My Nanna has retired at 75 and her colleagues put together a little leaving party for her and took some photos. My mum uploaded a Facebook post with said photos, supplemented with messages from our whole family. My Nanna started crying on the phone😭🥰💕
